item.title: 'I have done my duty': Harmanpreet Kaur steps down as India captain
item.description: India women’s captain Harmanpreet Kaur has stepped down from captaincy in all formats, bringing an end to her stint as the team’s leader. Harmanpreet said the decision was not easy but felt she had fulfilled her responsibility as captain.
item.dc:creator: AMIT KUMAR

item.title: Bengaluru gym trainer ‘strangled’ by collagues at anniversary party
item.description: M Nandan, a 25-year-old gym trainer, was allegedly assaulted to death after a quarrel among trainers. The incident occurred at a flat in Kempapura following the gym's anniversary celebration. Police have arrested three suspects involved in the assault, which reportedly escalated after consuming drugs and alcohol. Nandan's mother filed a complaint, leading to the investigation and arrests.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.dc:creator: AADRITA HALDER

item.title: Adam Neumann says a car ride with Masayoshi Son started WeWork's $47 billion collapse
item.description: WeWork co-founder Adam Neumann says the collapse of his $47 billion company began during a 30-minute car ride with SoftBank founder Masayoshi Son in 2016. Speaking on The Diary of a CEO podcast, Neumann said Son's $4.2 billion investment offer fed his ego and made it "about the money." He also discussed WeWork's failed IPO, Chapter 11 bankruptcy and his new real estate startup, Flow.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Four nations, four drills, one month: How the army is expanding its military partnerships
item.description: India is currently conducting simultaneous military exercises with multiple nations to strengthen defense relationships. Exercise Yudh Abhyas with the United States focuses on high-altitude warfare, while Exercise Mountain Guardian involves the UAE in mountain operations. KAZIND with Kazakhstan and Nomadic Elephant with Mongolia also highlight India's growing military diplomacy. These activities improve interoperability and expose Indian troops to diverse military practices.
item.dc:creator: DHRUV YADAV

item.title: Man gets flats under builder deal, transfers 5 to wife; gets Rs 4.14cr tax notice
item.description: The assessing officer made two major additions in this case. The first, Rs 1,93,78,293, was treated as long-term capital gains on the ground that the man had converted a capital asset into stock-in-trade. The second, of Rs 2,20,98,985, was treated as business income arising from the alleged sale of that stock-in-trade.
item.dc:creator: TOI BUSINESS DESK

item.title: Teen leaves home for ‘1L PUBG task’, found asleep on bus 3 days later
item.description: A 14-year-old student left his home in Firozabad to complete a PUBG gaming task. His family reported him missing after he failed to return home. Police used CCTV footage and mobile tracking to locate him three days later in Indore. Officers reunited the boy with his family and urged parents to monitor children's online activities. Previous incidents of children leaving home for gaming tasks have occurred in other regions.
item.dc:creator: MD. DILSHAD

item.title: 'More skeletons are tumbling out': Cong trains guns at EC over new report on Bengal polls
item.dc:creator: AASTHA JHA

item.title: Sujeet Kalkal on turning Olympic heartbreak into Asian Games gold
item.description: Sujeet Kalkal's Asian Games gold came two years after floods in Dubai cost him a chance to qualify for the Paris Olympics. The 25-year-old wrestler fought back from 2-9 down to beat Tajikistan's Abdulmazhid Kudiev 10-9 in the 65kg final, ending India's eight-year wait for a wrestling gold at the Games. Now targeting Los Angeles 2028, Kalkal says he does not want to go to the Olympics just to participate - he wants gold.
item.dc:creator: AMIT KUMAR

item.title: Soldiers searching for land mines find South Korea’s 600 years old gun
item.description: In a fascinating search for hidden landmines, South Korean troops discovered a small bronze gun buried beneath the earth. Dubbed a Hwangja Hwatong, this artifact dates back to the 14th or 15th century. The intricate details engraved on it can help historians piece together Korea's journey in firearm technology and military tactics from the times of the Goryeo and early Joseon dynasties.
item.dc:creator: TOI SCIENCE DESK

item.title: New Jersey wildlife centre cares for 219 box turtles dumped near river
item.description: The Mercer County Wildlife Center is diligently working to rehabilitate 219 abandoned box turtles, found near Cranford, New Jersey, back in July. A significant rescue operation was launched after these turtles were discovered by the riverbank. With winter on the horizon, the center is building outdoor enclosures to allow the turtles to brumate naturally.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: UIDAI announces new SOP for changing name on Aadhaar, here's what you need to know
item.description: UIDAI has introduced a revised Standard Operating Procedure for updating names in Aadhaar that began on September 18, 2026. The updated rules categorize name changes into minor and major with specific documentation requirements. Minor corrections can be made with standard proof of identity while significant changes need a Gazette Notification. Individuals can generally update their Aadhaar name twice before needing further approval.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Australian senator brings infant daughter to Parliament, speaks about motherhood
item.description: Fatima Payman made an impactful statement in Parliament, cradling her baby while sharing the often-overlooked trials of motherhood. She shed light on the emotional and physical hurdles faced during recovery post-childbirth, urging parents to seek the support they need without fear of judgment. Her message highlighted the importance of creating a more accommodating work environment for returning parents, resonating with many who juggle love and the real challenges of parenting.
item.dc:creator: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK

item.title: No missiles, no bullets: US picks 4 weapons to destroy drone swarms at light speed
item.description: The United States is set to assess four cutting-edge directed energy weapon systems designed specifically for drone defense. Under a new pilot program focused on directed energy, these technologies—prominently high energy lasers and high powered microwaves—will be tested. The goal is to bolster military proficiency by crafting robust counter-drone solutions, showcasing a strategic shift towards innovative approaches to combat emerging aerial threats.
item.dc:creator: ARYAN SINGH

item.dc:creator: AADRITA HALDER

item.title: Country Club promised plot with membership but never gave it; ordered to pay Rs 3.25L
item.description: A consumer commission in Delhi has ordered a hospitality club to reimburse a customer a sum of Rs 1.75 lakh after the club failed to deliver promised membership perks, including a complimentary plot in Maharashtra. In addition to the refund, the commission awarded Rs 1 lakh for mental distress and Rs 50,000 for legal costs.
item.dc:creator: SAURABH THAKUR

item.title: Fueling both sides? South Korea ships 150,000T fuel to Russia while funding Ukraine
item.description: In a nuanced twist, South Korea has been sending considerable quantities of diesel fuel to Russia even as it lends support to Ukraine amidst the ongoing invasion. Recent months have seen multiple shipments, indicating a complex dynamic between the two nations. Notably, this fuel trade continues despite South Korea's promise to aid Ukraine with essential military support and humanitarian assistance.
item.dc:creator: SHIVANGHI PAYAL

item.title: 'If SIR excludes citizens from voters list, what is its purpose?': Bombay HC to EC
item.description: Bombay High Court recently questioned the Election Commission regarding the removal of Indian citizens from electoral rolls. The court highlighted the importance of ensuring only citizens are on these rolls during special revisions. Justices emphasized that the process must not result in falsely excluding eligible voters. The Election Commission's guidelines and requirements for form submissions were scrutinized for being inadequate. The hearing on this matter will continue in subsequent sessions.
item.dc:creator: LISA MONTEIRO

item.title: Hardik Pandya's famous celebration returns, this time with MrBeast and CarryMinati
item.description: Hardik Pandya recently joined MrBeast and CarryMinati to recreate his iconic shrug celebration from the T20 World Cup. MrBeast visited India and shared his experiences, including photos with several celebrities. Pandya expressed his desire for MrBeast to return to India soon with a friendly message. The shrug celebration became famous after India's victory in the 2024 T20 World Cup final against South Africa.
item.dc:creator: AMIT KUMAR

item.title: Punjab govt to move SC against CBI probe into Mann's OSD over graft claims
item.dc:creator: AADRITA HALDER

item.title: Major fire guts labour camp outside Lucknow airport
item.description: A fire broke out at the temporary labor accommodation near Chaudhary Charan Singh International Airport, injuring two workers during the evacuation process. The blaze ignited around 6:50 am, swiftly overtaking the PVC panel structure. Firefighters successfully controlled the flames after 40 minutes, despite two explosions from LPG cylinders that occurred. Initial investigations revealed that the fire started while workers were cooking.
item.dc:creator: ARVIND CHAUHAN AND PATHIKRIT CHAKRABORTY

item.title: Russia plague scare puts US on watch as Rubio flags possible internal spread
item.description: A laboratory employee at Russia's Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute has tested positive for an infection, raising alarms over possible internal contagion. Marco Rubio, the US Secretary of State, noted that the US is actively observing the scenario as reported by Russian sources. Quarantine actions have been initiated, yet the exact infection details are not disclosed.
item.dc:creator: ARYAN SINGH

item.title: Cat meat trade: 2,700 cats stolen in Vietnam for meat; police bust suspected theft ring
item.description: In a shocking crackdown, police in Ho Chi Minh City apprehended a network of 12 individuals linked to an alarming cat theft and trafficking operation. Around 2,700 cats were reported stolen from local neighborhoods, with the suspects capturing these beloved pets under the cover of darkness to sell them as meat. The investigations unveiled a long-standing illegal operation, allowing authorities to act swiftly.
item.dc:creator: TIMESOFINDIA.COM

item.title: 'Taking medicines every day': How Humpy battled diarrhoea to win medals for India
item.description: In the sixth instalment of TimesofIndia.com's series looking back at India's medal-winning campaigns at the Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Koneru Humpy opens up about playing through illness to help the women's team win bronze. The 39-year-old reveals how diarrhoea and stomach pain forced her to take medicines and play almost every day. Humpy also discusses the physical demands of playing 10 of 11 rounds, Vaishali's struggles, her busiest stretch of the season and what lies ahead.
item.dc:creator: JYOTIRMOY HALDER

item.title: Lucknow floods: Why city got flooded days after the rain stopped
item.description: Lucknow has faced flooding in several neighborhoods due to upstream rainfall runoff. Local rainfall alone is not responsible for the resulting waterlogging in the city. Officials indicate that the runoff from upstream catchments has taken about eight to ten days to reach Lucknow. Urbanization and encroachment on the river's floodplain have exacerbated the flooding situation. Experts expect gradual improvement as runoff emissions begin to stabilize in the coming days.
item.dc:creator: ARVIND CHAUHAN

item.title: 86 to 101: Virat Kohli's final ODI window to break Tendulkar's century record
item.description: Virat Kohli is 15 centuries away from becoming the first batter to reach 101 international hundreds, with ODI cricket now his only route to Sachin Tendulkar's record. India have 11 confirmed bilateral ODIs before the 2027 World Cup, while the Asia Cup offers additional opportunities. A possible six-match South Africa series in the new FTP could give India further preparation before the World Cup, but the century chase remains a difficult one.
item.dc:creator: NITESH DUBEY

item.title: Woman declares Rs 67.4L ancestral jewellery in ITR; gets notice, she wins in ITAT
item.description: The assessment threw up two separate issues. The first concerned jewellery worth Rs 67,39,949 that the woman had disclosed in Schedule AL of her income tax return. The tribunal also examined whether the Rs 12 lakh paid to the HUF represented a genuine brokerage expense when the same person, the HUF's Karta/coparcener, had already received another Rs 12 lakh for the same transaction.
item.dc:creator: TOI BUSINESS DESK

item.title: Video: Staffer washes utensils in toilet at sweet shop; food dept issues notice
item.description: A video showing utensils being washed on a toilet floor at New Delhi Sweets raised significant concerns. The footage, shared on social media, prompted a food safety inspection by officials in Korba. During the inspection, the operator claimed this was due to an emergency water supply disruption. Food safety officer Sangharsh Kumar Mishra labeled the practice as unhygienic and a clear violation of norms.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Travis Kelce’s $5.35m mansion: Why does it have a $1.75m twin in Illinois?
item.description: Travis Kelce’s $5.35 million Ohio mansion, Moyenage, has a fascinating architectural connection to a $1.75 million home in Wheaton, Illinois. Both properties were designed by architect Jarvis Hunt for steel magnate Jay C. Morse, with the Ohio estate reportedly based on his earlier Illinois residence. The 10,000-square-foot House of Seven Gables retains historic details, including fireplaces, oak panelling, beamed ceilings and carved woodwork, despite being relocated in 2017.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: Naomi Osaka’s family mission: How did her Haitian roots inspire her work?
item.description: Naomi Osaka's heartfelt bond with Haiti is rooted in her family's foundation, which was formed in 1999 to uplift the community. Her inaugural trip to Haiti occurred in October 2017, followed by another visit after her first Grand Slam win in 2018. Engaging with local children, she championed educational initiatives and allocated part of her earnings for earthquake relief. This connection deeply influences Osaka's ongoing philanthropic endeavors.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: Before triple murder, Bengaluru techie used AI to ‘rehearse’ attack scenarios
item.description: In a shocking incident in Seegehalli, Bengaluru, techie J Kenneth allegedly murdered his partner's family. He had used artificial intelligence to research various methods of attack prior to the crime. Shwetha, Kenneth's partner, had borrowed substantial loans to support him, causing family tension. Following a confrontation with her parents about the loans, Kenneth reportedly carried out the violent act. Authorities continue to investigate the circumstances surrounding this tragic event.
item.dc:creator: RAJIV KALKOD

item.title: In Japan, women’s sumo battles tradition and a male-dominated system for survival
item.description: More than 100 women gathered at the Kyoto City Budo Centre to practice sumo wrestling. Despite historic resistance, female participation in sumo is increasing, with over 600 women involved in various clubs. The Japan Sumo Association does not recognise women's sumo, leaving many to rely on private clubs for training. Coaches and athletes express hope for future Olympic inclusion as they work to build awareness.
item.dc:creator: MANUJA VEERAPPA

item.title: Houthis target Aramco refinery, Saudi capital airport as Mecca defence pact activated
item.description: Yemen's Houthi rebels have claimed responsibility for missile and drone attacks targeting Saudi Arabia's infrastructure. The reported strikes included key sites such as airports and an Aramco refinery. In response, Saudi-backed Yemeni forces have intensified their offensive against the Houthis along the Red Sea coast. The conflict has prompted Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Türkiye to activate their defense pact for collective response.
item.dc:creator: ARYAN SINGH

item.title: Oil prices hover near $100 as Middle East supply holds up, Gulf risks persist
item.description: Oil prices are currently around $100 a barrel as stable Middle Eastern exports ease supply concerns. However, ongoing regional conflicts, including Houthi attacks, raise risks of disruptions. Officials indicate that rebuilding global oil stockpiles could take years due to significant withdrawals. Industry executives predict that demand recovery may not occur until 2028 or 2029. Prices may stabilize at around $70 a barrel depending on future production levels.
item.dc:creator: SHIVANGHI PAYAL

item.title: Trump signs order to ease diesel costs, ‘save millions of dollars’ for farmers
item.description: In response to rising diesel prices, US President Donald Trump has enacted an executive order designed to alleviate financial pressures across multiple sectors. This order is anticipated to substantially cut fuel costs for farmers and truck drivers, ultimately contributing to lower grocery prices. Additionally, it urges states to expand access to tax-free red-dyed diesel and consider lifting specific fuel taxes.
item.dc:creator: SHIVANGHI PAYAL

item.title: Trump blames Iran for flydubai incident, Vance 'defers', says 'nothing conclusively yet'
item.dc:creator: AASTHA JHA

item.title: Nepal ends flood search with over 5,000 still missing, including 189 Indians
item.description: Nepal has suspended non-essential search operations after the Bhotekoshi-Trishuli floods that occurred on August 26. The floods resulted in 1,455 deaths, with 5,285 people still unaccounted for, including many foreign tourists. Among the missing individuals are 189 Indians, along with tourists from various other countries. The government has shifted its focus towards reconstruction and rehabilitation efforts rather than continuing search operations.
item.dc:creator: VISHANT AGARWALA

item.title: Pakistan, Saudi, Turkiye activate Mecca defence pact as Yemen war escalates
item.description: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye have agreed to enhance military cooperation to address regional security threats. Following recent attacks by Yemen's Houthi group, the three countries will activate collective deterrence measures. The emergency meeting of the Mecca Defence Alliance in Riyadh led to this commitment. Saudi-backed forces are also launching an offensive against the Houthis in Yemen to regain control.
item.dc:creator: YASHASVI VASISTHA

item.title: Missed IIT by 0.01, rejected by MIT: Meet Perplexity’s Aravind Srinivas
item.description: Aravind Srinivas overcame significant educational hurdles after failing to meet the cut-off at IIT Madras. Taking charge of his learning, he self-taught programming and excelled in competitive challenges. Following successful internships at top AI research facilities, he co-founded Perplexity AI in 2022. Now, at just a young age, he boasts a remarkable net worth of $2.1 billion, showcasing his unwavering resilience and hard work.
item.dc:creator: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
